_comment: Fishing and crabbing (Fisheries, scripts/sim/fisheries.gd). families: the seafood commodities (data/markets.json lists them too, with their prices), base $ a ton landed, icon the species whose picture marks it in lists (the price menu). species: what's caught, each in a family, by a gear (troll: lines trolled behind small boats; net: gillnets and purse seines; trawl: big dragged nets; trap: crab pots), its price a ton the family's times grade; a trophy is one giant fish that fills a small trolling boat's hold on its own. grounds: where each species is caught and in which months (1-12), how thick the catch is there (density), how much the ground holds (stock_t: fishing draws it down, it regrows over a year), its depth (inshore grounds take every boat; offshore ones the tier 2 and 3 boats; deep ones only the tier 3), and the months its seas are rough (crabbing and fishing there wears boats harder: the Bering Sea in winter).

red_king_crab.name: Red king crab
red_king_crab.fact: The biggest catch of the Bering Sea's crab fleet: a leg span up to 1.8 m, fished in Bristol Bay each October in the worst seas in the world.

blue_king_crab.name: Blue king crab
blue_king_crab.fact: Brown with blue highlights, it lives round the Pribilofs and St. Matthew Island and turns red when cooked.

golden_king_crab.name: Golden king crab
golden_king_crab.fact: The deepest of the king crabs, caught year round off the Aleutians in pots set 300 to 1,000 m down.

southern_king_crab.name: Southern king crab (centolla)
southern_king_crab.fact: Centolla: Patagonia's king crab, fished from Punta Arenas and Ushuaia in the Strait of Magellan and the Beagle Channel.

snow_crab.name: Snow crab (opilio)
snow_crab.fact: Opilio: long thin legs, sweet meat; fished in winter on the Bering Sea ice edge and each spring in the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

tanner_crab.name: Tanner crab (bairdi)
tanner_crab.fact: Bairdi, the bigger Tanner crab of the Bering Sea and the Gulf of Alaska.

red_snow_crab.name: Red snow crab (beni-zuwai)
red_snow_crab.fact: Beni-zuwai: a deep red snow crab from the Sea of Japan, caught in pots set 500 to 2,500 m down.

hair_crab.name: Horsehair crab (kegani)
hair_crab.fact: Kegani, the horsehair crab: covered in short bristles, the prized winter crab of Hokkaido.

dungeness_crab.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness_crab.fact: The Pacific coast's crab, from Alaska to California: only males over 16 cm may be kept, and the season opens in December.

blue_crab.name: Atlantic blue crab
blue_crab.fact: Callinectes sapidus, 'beautiful swimmer': Chesapeake Bay's and Louisiana's crab, eaten as soft-shells when it moults.

stone_crab.name: Florida stone crab
stone_crab.fact: Only a claw is taken and the crab put back to grow another: Florida's stone crab season runs from October to May.

brown_crab.name: Brown crab (edible crab)
brown_crab.fact: The edible crab of Britain, Ireland and Norway: a pie-crust edge to its shell and black-tipped claws.

jonah_crab.name: Jonah crab
jonah_crab.fact: Once a by-catch of New England's lobster pots, now a fishery of its own.

atlantic_rock_crab.name: Atlantic rock crab
atlantic_rock_crab.fact: A small Cancer crab of Atlantic Canada and New England, freckled purple.

pacific_rock_crab.name: Pacific rock crab
pacific_rock_crab.fact: The red rock crab of the Pacific coast, with heavy black-tipped claws.

spider_crab.name: European spider crab
spider_crab.fact: Centolla in Spain, araignée in France: a spiny spider crab whose spring migration fills the Breton and Galician pots.

velvet_crab.name: Velvet swimming crab
velvet_crab.fact: A fierce little swimming crab with red eyes and a velvety blue-black shell, shipped live from Scotland to Spain.

spanner_crab.name: Spanner crab
spanner_crab.fact: Shaped like a spanner: it buries itself in the sand off Queensland and is caught on flat dillies, not pots.

gazami_crab.name: Gazami crab
gazami_crab.fact: The Japanese blue crab, the world's biggest crab catch by weight: over 300,000 tonnes a year from the Yellow and East China Seas.

blue_swimmer_crab.name: Blue swimmer crab
blue_swimmer_crab.fact: The flower crab of Southeast Asia and Australia, picked by hand in Thai and Filipino villages.

mud_crab.name: Mud crab
mud_crab.fact: The mangrove crab of the Indo-Pacific, with claws that can crush a finger: caught in the Sundarbans, Queensland and East Africa.

red_crab.name: Deep-sea red crab
red_crab.fact: A deep-sea crab of the New England slope, caught in pots 600 m down along the canyons.

golden_crab.name: Golden deep-sea crab
golden_crab.fact: A deep-water crab of the slope off Florida and the Carolinas, caught 300 to 700 m down.

giant_crab.name: Tasmanian giant crab
giant_crab.fact: One of the heaviest crabs in the world, up to 13 kg: caught in deep pots on the edge of Bass Strait.

skipjack.name: Skipjack tuna
skipjack.fact: The world's most-caught tuna: katsuobushi in Japan, trolled from small boats all through the tropical Pacific and Indian Ocean.

atlantic_salmon.name: Atlantic salmon
atlantic_salmon.fact: Trolled off Bornholm and in the Bothnian Sea each spring, and off West Greenland in late summer, as the salmon feed before running up their rivers.

spanish_mackerel.name: Spanish mackerel
spanish_mackerel.fact: Narrow-barred Spanish mackerel, seer fish in India, sawara in Japan, kingfish in the Gulf and sierra off Mexico: a fast, toothy mackerel trolled along warm coasts from the Red Sea to Shandong.

bluefish.name: Bluefish
bluefish.fact: Tailor in Australia, anchova in Brazil, lufer in Istanbul: a ferocious schooling predator that chops through the bait along every warm-temperate coast.

bonito.name: Bonito
bonito.fact: A small striped tuna: palamut running the Bosporus each autumn, bonito off California, Peru and the Canaries.

little_tunny.name: Little tunny (kawakawa)
little_tunny.fact: False albacore to Atlantic anglers, kawakawa in Hawaii: it blitzes the bait schools in autumn and fights hard for its size.

amberjack.name: Greater amberjack
amberjack.fact: The biggest of the jacks, up to 80 kg round reefs and wrecks: kampachi in Japan, ricciola in Italy.

sea_trout.name: Sea trout
sea_trout.fact: A brown trout that runs to sea: Baltic, Danish and Caspian boats troll for silver sea trout along the coasts in spring and autumn.

arctic_char.name: Arctic char
arctic_char.fact: The world's most northerly freshwater fish runs to sea each summer along Greenland, Svalbard, Siberia and the Canadian Arctic, red-bellied in its spawning colours.

pollack.name: Pollack
pollack.fact: Bronze-green and big-eyed, it hangs over the wrecks and kelp from Norway to Biscay and is trolled with lures over the reefs.

saithe.name: Saithe (coley)
saithe.fact: The pollack's northern cousin, schooling along Norway, the Faroes and Iceland and caught on feathers and pirks.

sea_bass.name: European sea bass
sea_bass.fact: Bar in France, branzino in Italy, levrek in Turkey: a silver predator of surf and estuary, trolled along the rocks of Brittany, Cornwall and the Mediterranean.

cobia.name: Cobia
cobia.fact: Shark-shaped and curious, cobia shadow the rays and buoys up the Gulf coast in spring and are the prize of the Chesapeake in summer.

red_drum.name: Red drum
red_drum.fact: Redfish: a copper drum with a black spot by its tail, schooling in the Gulf's passes and marshes each autumn.

queenfish.name: Queenfish
queenfish.fact: A leaping silver jack of Indo-Pacific shallows, trolled along reef edges and river mouths from the Gulf to northern Australia.

barramundi.name: Barramundi
barramundi.fact: Asian sea bass: born male and turning female as it grows, it runs the estuaries of northern Australia, India and South-East Asia in the wet season.

hairtail.name: Largehead hairtail
hairtail.fact: A silver ribbon of a fish with fangs: tachiuo in Japan, galchi in Korea, daiyu in China, the East China Sea's biggest catch, taken on lines at night.

lake_trout.name: Lake trout
lake_trout.fact: The Great Lakes' native char, deep-trolled from charter boats out of Duluth, Milwaukee and the Lake Ontario ports.

walleye.name: Walleye
walleye.fact: Named for its glassy eyes, built to hunt in murky water: Lake Erie is the walleye capital of the world, trolled with crankbaits all summer.

snoek.name: Snoek
snoek.fact: A long, toothy barracouta of the cold Benguela, caught by the Cape's line boats each winter and smoked or braaied.

australian_salmon.name: Australian salmon (kahawai)
australian_salmon.fact: Not a salmon at all but a big sea perch, running in huge schools along the beaches of southern Australia and New Zealand each autumn.

northern_pike.name: Northern pike
northern_pike.fact: In the brackish Baltic and the Siberian estuaries the pike lives in the sea, hunting the reed beds and the archipelagos.

rainbow_runner.name: Rainbow runner
rainbow_runner.fact: A sleek jack striped blue and yellow, it hunts with the tuna round tropical reefs and floating logs.

dogtooth_tuna.name: Dogtooth tuna
dogtooth_tuna.fact: The reef tuna: it lives on the drop-offs of Indo-Pacific atolls, with conical teeth no other tuna has, and pulls anglers straight into the coral.

coral_trout.name: Coral trout
coral_trout.fact: Red with blue spots, the Great Barrier Reef's most prized eating fish, trolled deep along the reef edges and sold live to Hong Kong.

snook.name: Snook
snook.fact: Robalo: a black-lined silver predator of mangroves and river mouths from Florida to Brazil, and on the Pacific side from Mexico to Peru.

spotted_seatrout.name: Spotted seatrout
spotted_seatrout.fact: Speckled trout: the Gulf coast's favourite fish, trolled over the grass flats of Texas, Louisiana and Florida.

kob.name: Kob (meagre)
kob.fact: A big croaker that drums underwater: meagre in the Mediterranean and off Mauritania, kob in South Africa, mulloway in Australia, up to 2 m long.

leerfish.name: Leerfish (garrick)
leerfish.fact: A deep-bodied jack of the Mediterranean and South Africa's estuaries, trolled with live mullet in summer.

dentex.name: Dentex
dentex.fact: A big toothy sea bream of the Mediterranean's rocky shores, trolled with live squid over the drop-offs; one of its finest eating fish.

lingcod.name: Lingcod
lingcod.fact: Neither a ling nor a cod, this big-mouthed greenling of the Pacific rocks from Alaska to California can have blue-green flesh.

rockfish.name: Rockfish
rockfish.fact: A hundred kinds of spiny, colourful rockfish live off the Pacific coast; some live over 200 years.

japanese_sea_bass.name: Japanese sea bass
japanese_sea_bass.fact: Suzuki in Japan, nongeo in Korea, luyu in China: a silver estuary bass trolled along the coasts and river mouths of East Asia.

snapper.name: Pink snapper
snapper.fact: Tamure to the Maori: Australia's and New Zealand's favourite reef fish, pink with blue spots and a bump on its head when old.

grouper.name: Grouper (hamour)
grouper.fact: Hamour in the Gulf, garoupa in Hong Kong, gag in Florida: a big-mouthed reef bass, the most prized fish on many tropical coasts.

muskellunge.name: Muskellunge
muskellunge.fact: The fish of ten thousand casts: the giant pike of the St. Lawrence and the Great Lakes, trolled for in autumn.

smallmouth_bass.name: Smallmouth bass
smallmouth_bass.fact: Bronzebacks: the Great Lakes' hardest-fighting fish, over the rocky reefs of Lake Erie and Lake Ontario all summer.

garfish.name: Garfish
garfish.fact: A needle-nosed fish with green bones, arriving in the Baltic, the North Sea and the Black Sea with the spring; trolled with tiny lures as it skitters over the surface.

mangrove_jack.name: Mangrove jack
mangrove_jack.fact: A red snapper of the mangroves and estuaries of northern Australia, India and South-East Asia, that bolts for the snags when hooked.

antarctic_toothfish.name: Antarctic toothfish
antarctic_toothfish.fact: Antifreeze in its blood keeps it alive at -2 C; scientists at McMurdo have caught them through holes in the sea ice for decades, and they grow to 2 m.

marbled_rockcod.name: Marbled rockcod
marbled_rockcod.fact: A blotchy Antarctic cod of the South Shetlands and the Peninsula, caught on handlines from the station boats in the short summer.

zander.name: Zander
zander.fact: Pikeperch: trolled in the Caspian, the Black Sea's lagoons and the Baltic's bays; its white flesh is prized from Finland to Iran.
